_about: Timber unload ramps at a fixed-grip chair's top return terminal (task 4.50 phase 4; bldgkit/unload_ramp.py builds them). Owner 2026-11-24: an unload 5 ft or more over the ground gets this ramp (under 5 ft the game grades an earth mound of the same shape; a top drive gets none); it clips into the terrain, so no railings or walls; double wide like the photos: one deck centred on the lift across both ropes and one ski-off ramp past the bullwheel, flaring 1 in 10 per side, with no ramp back down the line. One model for every lift, whatever its maker and wherever it stands; only the chair's width changes it, so three models (quad, triple, double), and clipping makes that work: the ramp is built for its tallest site (`reach`) and the terrain clips it, and the lift's terminal stands through the plain deck. Approved (plans 2 to 4, 30 % at Gate 1): 4.5 m level deck, the ramp at 30 % (the code's limit), up-side widths 3.6 / 3.0 / 2.4 m (8.8 / 7.6 / 6.4 m in all), a hut bay where the hut stands in its own opening on its own steel posts, a mat as wide as the chair and the operator's pedestal (oppedestal.json); no light pole and no signs, and the stop gate is a post and bar past the wheel, its own model (stopgate.json); a 42 in timber rail round the hut bay; $600 per m2 of deck above the ground plus $2k. Ramp frame in the builder's docstring. Millimetres.

terminals._about: Each top return terminal, measured on its lift model (ramp frame, from the unload point; the same for its quad, triple and double): `wheelU` the bullwheel's axle past the unload point (it places the stop gate); `gateFace` the front face of the column that holds up the bullwheel, on the lift's centreline (the stop gate's post stands at least 0.3 m past it); `through` what stands through the deck [u from, u to, half width about the lift's centreline]; `under` what lies just under it [.., top]. The deck's boards and joists clip round them; no post or beam comes within `keepClear` of any of them, for every terminal at once.

reach._about: the tallest site the model serves (the deck over the natural ground) and the ski-off's run as modelled: 6 m down at 30 %, which meets level ground 4 m down after 13.3 m and ground falling 15 % from 3 m down after 20 m; past that the game fills under the toe

deck._about: the deck boards run across the deck and the ramp, 7 a metre, drawn by the lift atlas's planks detail tile on one face per deck cell (owner 2026-11-24: texture, not modelled boards)

posts._about: `below` how far posts run under the tallest site's ground; `brace` how far down each row's diagonals reach; `clear` how far posts and beams keep from a terminal

gate._about: the stop gate (stopgate.json, its own model per terminal style) is a post on the ramp past the unload on the lift's centreline and a bar from its top along the line, `under` below the chair's lowest point and at least `least` over the deck, the ramp or the ground all the way; the bar covers where the chair's seat crosses the line round the far end of the wheel, from `before` inside its inner end to `past` beyond its outer end; the post stands `postClear` inside the chair's inner end (owner 2026-11-24: inward, clear of the turning chairs, the doubles too)

hutBay._about: for the mini hut (a fixed grip's return): the deck is framed round the hut's footprint (`hut`, `gap` clear), the hut stands in it on four steel pipe posts of its own down to the ground, its floor (`floor` over the hut's origin, `base` thick) a `threshold` above the deck; the hut's skids and step (its `legs` part) are hidden; `width` ends the bay flush with the hut's back wall (`hutV` + half the hut, owner 2026-11-24)

rail._about: the level deck's timber guard rail (owner 2026-11-24): 4x4 posts at most `pitch` apart, their outer faces `inset` inside the deck's edge, a 2x6 top rail laid flat at `height` (42 in, the US rule for a guard rail on a work platform: 39-45 in) and a 2x4 mid rail at `midAt` (about halfway), round the bay's open edges from the walkway's top to the hut and from the hut to the up side's outer edge; and (`returnSide`) along the return side's outer edge, opposite the hut, for the level deck's length; the walkway and the ski-off ramp get none

lip._about: the deck's lip (owner 2026-11-24): a 2x4 laid flat on the boards [across, tall], its outer face flush with the edge, along every edge with no rail: both sides of the ski-off ramp and the rear edge, but not across the lane where the riders' skis come in (the mat's width)

walkway._about: the operator's walkway up from the snow (owner 2026-11-24): the ski-off ramp carries on `width` further on the hut side at the same slope and flare, one ramp, and that outer strip has a cleat across it every `pitch` from `from` past the breakover; 30 % is within the US work-platform rule for a walkway (1 in 3 at most, `slopeMax`; cleats at most 14 in apart above 1 in 8, `pitchMax`)

pedestal._about: where the operator's pedestal (bldg_op_pedestal) stands on the hut bay, from the unload point and the up side's outer edge

common._seat: the rope 3,039 over the lift's 0.00 load/unload level (the deck); `chairBelowRope` the chair frame's lowest point (379 over the deck), `seatBelowRope` the top of the seat's pad at mid-depth (the Sessellift chair's seat sockets; 500 over the deck, 444 at the back, 550 at the front edge), the code's chair height, at most `seatMax` (22 in)

photos._about: Gate 2 stills (render_ramp_cases.render_photos; owner 2026-11-24: all three versions, quad, triple and double), each width at another maker's terminal: [shot, view, mode]
